title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. This page belongs to the 'variations sur l'équation des lacets' (the loop equations). Grothendieck is describing the elements u of a local automorphism group of the profinite fundamental groupoid of M_{0,3} = P^1 - {0,1,∞}. On the next page this group is called Aut_loc(Ĉ^+_{0,3}, σ_∞)'. These u commute with σ_∞, the order-2 symmetry exchanging 0 and 1 and fixing ∞, and they are compatible with ρ, the order-3 rotation of {0,1,∞}.

Notation. l_0 and l_1 are the inertia loops at 0 and 1. On the previous page he set:
- γ = (p-1)/2 ∈ Ẑ, where p = χ(u) ∈ Ẑ* is the cyclotomic character;
- h_0 = g_0^{-1}σ_∞(g_0);
- g = σ_∞(g_0) l_1^γ ρ(g_0)^{-1}, formula (62);
- ξ = l_0^γ h_0.
The condition (51) on g then became the 'cocycle for ρ' relation ξ ρ(ξ) ρ²(ξ) = 1, which is (64).

What this page does.
(i) It records that u is parametrized by pairs (g_0 ∈ π̂_{0,3}/L_0, γ ∈ Ẑ) subject to two conditions: 2γ+1 ∈ Ẑ*, and a single equation in g_0, namely the boxed (65). In (65), (64) is written out with ξ = l_0^γ g_0^{-1}σ_∞(g_0). The 'boundary conditions' (53) are set aside 'pour mémoire'.
(ii) It switches to the parametrization by (ξ, γ). From ξ one recovers h_0 = l_0^{-γ}ξ, and then g_0 from g_0^{-1}σ_∞(g_0) = h_0. This rests on two provisional assumptions:
- Uniqueness of g_0 holds because π̂_{0,3}^{σ_∞} = {1}. If g_0^{-1}σ(g_0) = g_1^{-1}σ(g_1), then g_1 g_0^{-1} is σ-fixed.
- Existence of g_0 is equivalent to the 2-cocycle condition σ_∞(h_0) h_0 = 1, which is (67). This is the vanishing of the nonabelian H^1(Z/2, π̂_{0,3}) for the σ_∞-action.
(iii) Condition (67), rewritten in terms of ξ and γ, gives (68) on the next page: σ_∞(ξ) = l_1^γ ξ^{-1} l_0^γ.

Modern dictionary. Write λ = 2γ+1 and m = (λ-1)/2 = γ. Then the system (63) + (64) + (68) is the profinite Grothendieck–Teichmüller system of Drinfeld and Ihara:
- λ ∈ Ẑ*;
- the 2-cycle relation f(x,y) f(y,x) = 1, here 'twisted' because ξ = l_0^γ h_0;
- the hexagon (3-cycle) relation f(z,x) z^m f(y,z) y^m f(x,y) x^m = 1.
Here h_0 plays the role of f. The ρ-equation is cast as a Z/3-cocycle condition and the σ-equation as a Z/2-cocycle condition. g_0 is a Z/2 'trivializing cochain' for f, i.e. f = g^{-1}σ(g). This turns the two GT relations into one equation in g_0. On the next page the ρ-relation is likewise trivialized parametrically, with two cases ξ = λρ(λ)^{-1} or λ l_0^{-1} ρ(λ)^{-1}.
errors: No algebraic error. Check: σ(h_0)h_0 = σ(g_0)^{-1} g_0 g_0^{-1} σ(g_0) = 1 because σ_∞² = 1. Substituting h_0 = l_0^{-γ}ξ and σ_∞(l_0) = l_1 indeed gives σ_∞(ξ) = l_1^γ ξ^{-1} l_0^γ.

Gap, acknowledged by Grothendieck: the two facts used are 'admitted provisionally'. These are π̂_{0,3}^{σ_∞} = 1 and the vanishing of nonabelian H^1(Z/2, π̂_{0,3}), i.e. every σ-cocycle is a coboundary. For the discrete free group both are elementary. π_1 ⋊ Z/2 ≅ Z * Z/2, and involutions in a free product are conjugate into a factor. Profinitely they follow from the Herfort–Ribes theorem (1985) on finite subgroups of free profinite products. Note also that g_0 is only defined in π̂_{0,3}/L_0, so h_0 is only defined up to the twist h_0 ↦ l_0^{-1}h_0 l_1. That twist reappears as the ambiguity (69) on the next page; uniqueness 'de façon unique' should be read with this in mind.
The boundary ('limitrophe') conditions (53) are explicitly deferred, so the parametrization is incomplete as stated.

ideas.what: Parametrization of the automorphisms u by (λ = 2γ+1 ∈ Ẑ*, ξ) satisfying the 3-cycle relation ξρ(ξ)ρ²(ξ) = 1 and the twisted 2-cycle relation σ(ξ) = l_1^γ ξ^{-1} l_0^γ, with γ = (λ-1)/2.
ideas.modern_name: Defining relations of the profinite Grothendieck–Teichmüller group GT^ (relations I and II, with m = (λ-1)/2)
ideas.where_published: Not in Esquisse or the published Longue Marche excerpts as explicit equations, as far as I know (unsure about the full Longue Marche text).

ideas.what: Trivializing the 2-cycle relation: h_0 with σ(h_0)h_0 = 1 is written as h_0 = g_0^{-1}σ_∞(g_0). Uniqueness comes from trivial fixed points and existence from vanishing of nonabelian H^1(Z/2, π̂_{0,3}). This turns the GT system into a single 'equation in g_0'.
ideas.modern_name: Nonabelian Galois-type cohomology H^1(Z/2, F̂_2) = 1 / coboundary parametrization of the 2-cycle relation
ideas.usually_credited_to: unsure; the cohomological input follows from Herfort–Ribes (torsion in free profinite products)

ideas.what: Viewing the GT relations as cocycle conditions for the S_3-symmetries (σ of order 2, ρ of order 3) of P^1 - {0,1,∞} acting on π̂_1. The next page gives the parametric solutions of the order-3 cocycle, with two classes.
ideas.modern_name: Cocycle/torsor interpretation of GT relations; nonabelian H^1(Z/3, F̂_2) with two classes (cf. PSL_2(Z) = Z/2 * Z/3)

missed.claim: Grothendieck proposes replacing the GT system by a single 'equation in g_0'. This is (65): (l_0^γ g_0^{-1}σ(g_0)) ρ(...) ρ²(...) = 1, with g_0 ∈ π̂_{0,3}/L_0. The 2-cycle relation is thereby built in through a nonabelian-H^1 trivialization. As far as I know this single-equation reformulation of GT^ via a Z/2-coboundary has not been systematically exploited.
missed.quote: ("équation en g_0" — par opposition avec l'"équation en ζ" plus bas)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It gives an alternative coordinate system on GT^ (and on GRT / associators by analogy) in which relation (I) disappears. That could simplify computations of GT^ or its pro-unipotent and pro-ℓ versions.

missed.claim: The provisionally admitted facts are π̂^{σ}=1 and H^1(Z/2, π̂_{0,3}) = 1, together with the two-case parametrization of the Z/3-cocycle on the next page. These are exactly consequences of the profinite Kurosh/Herfort–Ribes theory for F̂_2 ⋊ Z/2 and F̂_2 ⋊ Z/3 (free products such as Z/2 * Z/3 ≅ PSL_2(Z)). Grothendieck's notes thus link the GT relations to torsion/conjugacy theory in free profinite products, a link not usually stated in the GT literature.
missed.quote: puisqu'on fait (qu'on admet provisoirement) que π̂_{0,3}^{σ_∞} = {1}. La possibilité de trouver g_0 satisfaisant à cette condition équivaut (on l'admettra aussi ici) à la condition σ_∞(h_0)h_0 = 1
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It gives a conceptual cohomological reason for the shape of the GT relations and their parametric solutions. It might generalize to the higher M_{0,n} relations (pentagon) via finite subgroups of mapping class groups.

deep.surprise_reason: The page shows Grothendieck independently arriving, in the early 1980s, at the GT^ relations with exactly Drinfeld's m = (λ-1)/2, plus a cohomological single-equation reformulation via g_0. Specialists know vaguely that the Longue Marche anticipates GT, but this explicit computation and the H^1-trivialization trick are not, to my knowledge, in the record. Still, it is a computational step largely subsumed by Drinfeld/Ihara.
transcription_corrections: The Greek letter written 'ζ' throughout this page is the same symbol ξ used on the neighbouring pages (ξ = l_0^γ h_0).
'puisqu'on fait (qu'on admet provisoirement)' should probably read 'puisqu'on sait (qu'on admet provisoirement)'.
'la condition liminaire, pour mémoire' is likely 'la condition limitrophe, pour mémoire', consistent with 'conditions limitrophes' on the next page.
'équivaut (on l'admettra aussi ici) : la condition' should read 'équivaut (on l'admettra aussi ici) à la condition'.
The boxed equation's label appears overwritten (possibly '(65 bis)' corrected to '(65)').
The left marginal note is roughly: 'il conviendrait d'appeler cette ... "équation en ξ" ... "équation en h_0" ... "équation en g_0" (62)'. It is uncertain; it concerns renaming the equations.
